whatThisRecordIs: The public-safe aggregate of an inventory built entirely in a separate private workspace. Every figure here is a count over material this repository does not hold and may not hold, taken from one clean run of that workspace's own gate on its settled tree, and every one of them was re-derived here from the underlying rows rather than read off that gate's summary. The files those counts came from are bound below by digest, and that binding is for a reader who holds the private workspace and hashes it: nothing in this repository recomputes those digests, because the files are not here.

graph.blockedNodeReason: declared no dependency metadata, so the node exists and its edges are unknown rather than absent

reads.whyNotSix: An earlier form of this figure counted six producers. The sixth was the surface recount, which the code itself does not call a producer, and an independent round found the line saying so. Five producers and the recount are watched; the figure is written as the two things it is rather than as one number that was wrong.

readObservation.watches: Two wrapped channels — four methods of Python's zipfile, and the unzip binary shimmed ahead of the real one on PATH — plus, since the repair, a second reading of the premise itself: a scan computes what the gate reaches, sweeps it for read primitives, and requires every occurrence to be routed through a watched channel or accounted for by name.
readObservation.bound: The premise that the wrapped channels were the only channels used to be asserted in the file installing the wrappers and checked by nothing. An independent round falsified it: a reader using only unwatched standard library calls decompressed 50357 class files and wrote their bytecode to disk while the gate exited zero and printed that no entry bodies had been read. That is repaired. The premise now gets a second reading rather than an assertion, the interpreter shim resolves the script it is pointed at instead of accounting for a variable, and twelve mutations across seven channels now exit nonzero. What the repair does not claim is the important part, and it is stated here rather than left to be discovered: see uncaughtCase below.
readObservation.notWatched: Reads of files that are not archives — the pinned manifest, the acquisition log, the workspace's own tracked files and the pack override tree. The primitive scan additionally reads static text, so a name computed at run time is opaque to it, it never reads text a run generates, and it recognises only the primitives its vocabulary names, so a channel nobody has thought of is invisible until somebody adds a row.
readObservation.uncaughtCase: One mutation still exits zero, and it is disclosed rather than hidden. A fully coordinated hand that deletes a primitive's refusal row, injects the reader, and writes its occurrence rows in the same edit passes, because the accounted half is a table and a table records what it is told. It leaves a tell rather than a failure: the gate's own line visibly reports one fewer refused primitive than it should. That is a tell, not a check, and it is not claimed as caught. This catches an accident and a careless hand; it does not catch a determined one. docs/decisions/claims-without-a-second-reading.md is the record governing a claim of exactly this shape, and the obligation it imposes — that a mechanism state what it does not catch, in the file that acts on the claim and in what it prints — is met: the private gate prints its own limits on every run, pass or fail, and emptying that disclosure is itself a failure.

judgedClaims.claim: the licence family each distinct declared licence string belongs to
judgedClaims.recordedIn: a tracked table of one row per distinct declared string
judgedClaims.whyNoSecondReading: nothing about a licence is derivable from the artifact it governs, so a mutation changing the classifying code and the table together passes

judgedClaims.claim: the source-use verdict each licence family carries
judgedClaims.recordedIn: a tracked table of one row per family, each row carrying its reason
judgedClaims.whyNoSecondReading: this is the decision that moves artifacts between prohibited and cleared, and it sits one function below the family test; flipping one line moves 65 artifacts without moving a single family

judgedClaims.claim: whether an author reserved their assets apart from their code
judgedClaims.recordedIn: a column beside each distinct declared string
judgedClaims.whyNoSecondReading: a reservation is a statement in prose the author wrote, and no count over the artifact contradicts a wrong reading of it

primitiveScan.holds: Every read primitive occurring in what the private gate reaches must be routed through a watched channel or accounted for by name with a reason. The vocabulary is congruent three ways: each declared pattern must match the probe recorded beside it, an accounted primitive that nothing uses is stale and fails, and the occurrence table and the vocabulary must name the same primitives in both directions.
